# Clanky iOS - Full Docs

> Clanky iOS is the native SwiftUI client for attaching to the Eve relay, inspecting herdr state, and steering Clanky work from a phone without inventing a second API.

Generated from the live docs site. Each section below is one page; see the heading and source path for context.

---

# Overview

Source: `README.md` - https://volpestyle.github.io/docs/clanky-ios/?doc=overview

# Clanky iOS

Native SwiftUI window for checking and steering Clanky from an iPhone. The app
talks to the Eve relay that Clanky starts locally, mirrors the live herdr
workspace/tab/pane hierarchy, and sends operator input back through the same
relay contract used by the desktop tools.

## What You Can Do

- connect to an Eve relay over local network or Tailscale
- store the relay URL in app preferences and the relay bearer token in Keychain
- generate and store an ed25519 SSH lifecycle key in Keychain
- run `scripts/clanky-up.ts` over SSH in `up`, `status`, and `down` modes
- inspect herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, agents, and recent terminal output
- send text and special keys to a pane through `run` and `keys` relay ops
- launch and close herdr panes through the Clanky relay
- start or continue a chat-with-Clanky Eve session

## Contract Boundary

This repository is the SwiftUI client only. The canonical API is the current
Clanky implementation in `../clanky`, especially:

- `SPEC.md` for the iOS window behavior
- `scripts/clanky-up.ts` for lifecycle bootstrap output
- `agent/channels/relay.ts` for relay operations and payloads
- `agent/lib/frontdoor-auth.ts` for bearer-token auth
- Eve session routes for chat-with-Clanky conversation state

When the app needs new behavior, update or document the Clanky contract first,
then wire the iOS integration against that contract.

## Mental Model

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  phone["Clanky iOS"]
  network["LAN / Tailscale"]
  sshd["sshd"]
  lifecycle["scripts/clanky-up.ts"]
  eve["Eve front door"]
  relay["/relay/ws"]
  herdr["herdr workspace"]
  session["/eve/v1/session"]

  phone --> network
  network --> sshd
  network --> eve
  sshd --> lifecycle
  lifecycle --> herdr
  lifecycle --> eve
  eve --> relay
  eve --> session
  relay --> herdr
```

HTTP URLs are accepted for local/private LAN and Tailscale modes. Custom public
endpoints should use HTTPS.

## Connect

On first launch, copy the app's SSH public key from the connection screen and
add it to the Mac user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Then enter the Mac SSH host,
user, port, Clanky repo path, relay URL, and relay token.

The app runs this lifecycle command over SSH before attaching to the relay:

```bash
cd <repoPath> && CLANKY_RELAY_TOKEN=<token> node scripts/clanky-up.ts --json
```

The `status` and `down` lifecycle modes are available from the connected room
actions sheet.

The app also accepts deep links of the form:

```text
clanky://connect?relayUrl=http://127.0.0.1:2000&token=...
```

For local simulator development, leaving SSH host empty still lets the app
attach to an already-running relay.

## Run

```bash
brew install xcodegen      # if not already installed
xcodegen generate
open ClankyIOS.xcodeproj
```

Command line:

```bash
xcodebuild -project ClankyIOS.xcodeproj \
  -scheme ClankyIOS \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' \
  build
```

## Documentation

The hosted docs UI renders this README as the source of truth.

```bash
pnpm docs:dev
pnpm docs:build
```

## Structure

```text
ClankyIOS/
  ClankyIOSApp.swift
  RootView.swift
  Tokens/
  Models/
  Components/
  Screens/
  Services/
```

The seeded `AppStore.demo()` workspace uses Clanky/herdr sample data so the
window hierarchy can be inspected before connecting to a live relay.
